review_notes: I read the whole file. I checked the only large repeated blocks, which are hb' and ha' in exists_v (lines 233-252). I compared them with res_u'_eq, which uses the same F_res_apply / ← map_pull / homOfLE_comp finish but is not otherwise parallel. I also saw the same two-line d_apply expansions in d_u' and exists_v, and the duplicated hcoc statement in `main` and `solution`. I judged those too short or too thin to report. The proposed helper is untested. Its hypothesis shape, in particular the unification of `face … k = idx0 c` and the dependent `Fin 2` index, may need small adjustments when it is compiled.

findings.problem: hb' and ha' are the same ~10-line argument, instantiated at (face 0, b, inf_le_right, face_idx1_zero) and (face 1, a, inf_le_left, face_idx1_one). Each one (1) uses res_at_eq to replace the face index by idx0 c, (2) uses res_res to merge two restrictions into the one coming from pre_le_inter_idx0 c, (3) unfolds the definition of w c, (4) rewrites with hv c, F_res_apply and ← map_pull, and (5) collapses the composite restrictions with homOfLE_comp. The duplicated side-conditions `hle2.trans (((Opens.map U.ι.base).monotone inf_le_right).trans …)` and the `res_res` arguments are long, so the copies are easy to get out of sync. The step that reuses the same transport-of-restriction reasoning in res_u'_eq (lines 134-137) is a third near-instance.
findings.proposed_change:
Add, before exists_v, a lemma such as

theorem res_face_idx1 (v' : (F N U).cochain (cover U P hPU haff hcov) 0) {a b c : ι} (hab : a < b) (k : Fin 2)
    (hk : (cover U P hPU haff hcov).face (idx1 U P hPU haff hcov hab) k = idx0 U P hPU haff hcov c)
    (hc : P2 P a b ≤ P c) (vc : Γ(N, P c))
    (hvc : pull U.ι N (P c) vc = (F N U).res (pre_le_inter_idx0 U P hPU haff hcov c) (v' (idx0 U P hPU haff hcov c))) :
    (F N U).res ((cover U P hPU haff hcov).inter_le_inter_face (idx1 U P hPU haff hcov hab) k)
        (v' ((cover U P hPU haff hcov).face (idx1 U P hPU haff hcov hab) k))
      = ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.ι).obj N).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inter_idx1 U P hPU haff hcov hab).le).op
          (pull U.ι N (P2 P a b) (N.presheaf.map (homOfLE hc).op vc))

Proof sketch: this is the current body of hb', with b replaced by c, inf_le_right by hc and face_idx1_zero by hk. First apply res_at_eq with hk, then ← res_res, then `change … (F N U).res _ (… c)`, then rewrite ← hvc, F_res_apply, ← map_pull, and finish with the homOfLE_comp simp.

The two uses then become

have hb' := res_face_idx1 N U P hPU haff hcov v' hab 0 (face_idx1_zero U P hPU haff hcov hab) inf_le_right (v b) (hv b).symm
have ha' := res_face_idx1 N U P hPU haff hcov v' hab 1 (face_idx1_one U P hPU haff hcov hab) inf_le_left (v a) (hv a).symm

The hypotheses of exists_v are unchanged. `hv b : pull … (v b) = w b` is by definition the right-hand side of hvc, because w is a `let`. The later `rw [hb', ha'] at hcomp` is then unaffected.
findings.benefit: The delicate restriction-compatibility argument is written and checked once instead of twice. exists_v then shows only the mathematical content: the two faces of the 1-simplex restrict to the pulled-back v b and v a. The ~20 lines of proof with heavy `Opens.map U.ι.base` monotonicity side-goals shrink to two one-line applications. A future change to the cover or to idx0/idx1 needs one edit instead of two parallel ones.
